# XDVDFS reader origin

The adapter uses antangelo's MIT-licensed [`xdvdfs` 0.8.3](https://crates.io/crates/xdvdfs/0.8.3) for the Xbox DVD volume and directory layouts, Windows-1252 decoding and case comparison. The official crates.io archive has SHA-256 `1777c1ccae32a2185ac98adae015aed3fb06242084b5e7f8b08a811fe0e7b936` and comes from [revision `1cc850bf1b3487fad7ec7c9eed01d83e8fc75ba4`](https://github.com/antangelo/xdvdfs/tree/1cc850bf1b3487fad7ec7c9eed01d83e8fc75ba4). The adapter adds bounded reads, cycle and overlap checks, on-demand range reads and the host's read-only filesystem contract.

The fixture `tests/fixtures/extract-xiso.zlib` decompresses to the 851,968 bytes emitted by [XboxDev/extract-xiso revision `3f5b62cfe68f000b0e3c8a30104973f3a297948e`](https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso/tree/3f5b62cfe68f000b0e3c8a30104973f3a297948e) using `extract-xiso -q -m -c fixture-files extract-xiso-native.iso` on Linux. Its raw SHA-256 is `565f5c8c0efb48a6f38ecaffcde9510cd401772bbb2340550ef5d7735d36046c`. All input files were generated for these tests. The C tool is used for fixture construction and verification only. The CLI test places the independent game partition at each XGD offset, with a separately constructed ISO 9660 prefix for XGD3.
